verse.text: “Therefore I tell you, do not worry about your life, what you will eat or drink; or about your body, what you will wear. Is not life more than food, and the body more than clothes?

reflection.scripture: “Therefore I tell you, do not worry about your life, what you will eat or drink; or about your body, what you will wear. Is not life more than food, and the body more than clothes?
reflection.observation: Jesus is speaking to a crowd anxious about survival — food, clothing, basic needs. He doesn't dismiss their concerns as trivial; He reframes them. Life is more than the sum of its provisions. The word 'Therefore' ties this to what came before: you can't serve both God and money (v. 24). Worry is a form of divided loyalty. Jesus isn't saying 'stop caring' — He's asking, 'Do you trust the One who gave you life to sustain it?'
reflection.application: What am I worrying about today that reveals where my trust actually lies? Is it a bill, a health concern, a relationship? Write down one specific worry, then write one truth about God's character that directly counters it. Example: 'I'm worried about finances' → 'God knows my needs before I ask' (v. 8). Make this a daily practice in SOAPaDay — one worry, one truth.
reflection.prayer: Lord, I confess that my worries often feel more real than Your promises. Today I bring You my specific concern: ________. Help me see that You are not distant from my needs — You are the source of everything I have. Teach me to seek Your kingdom first, trusting that the rest follows. Amen.
